title: Igulim and yosher: the dream that surrounds everything, and the deed that rules it
overview:
The *Kav* goes down from the *reshimu*, circles, goes down and circles again: the *igulim* are one line. In them the highest surrounds all and is best, and the innermost is lowest; in *yosher* it is the other way around. To see why, the chapter looks at the *ratzon kadum*, the original will. It is revealed compared to the *ratzon hamuchlat*, but still hidden and for oneself, like the stirring to have things your own way before you know it means a house, and it already holds every detail, down to the bathroom drapes. In the *Zohar*'s words it is *Atika d'Atikin*, and in the *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon*, *Atika Stima'a*; the delight already in *chachma*, in *Atzilus*, is *Atika Kadisha*.

In the circles every cause surrounds its effect, and the effect never reaches it, as a kid's reasons never capture why he wants a bike. When the will comes to be done in actual fact, it reverses: will hides in intellect, intellect in *middos*, *middos* in the deed, and the *sof maaseh* becomes king. *Igulim* are *teshuva*, *yosher* good deeds. Of the Essence above the *Kav* nothing can be said: the *tzimtzum* is a jump, not a line.

terms.gloss: circles: the sefiros one inside the other, where the outermost, the will, is the main thing and everything inside is a token of it
the straight line: the sefiros enclothed one in the lower one in the shape of a person, where the deed is on the outside and on top
the original (not merely first) will: the origin of every detail, revealed compared to the ratzon hamuchlat but still hidden and for oneself
the final deed: in the circles the flimsiest daydream and the innermost; in yosher the top thing that everything has to fit
the Atik of all Atiks: the ratzon kadum as the inner pleasure behind all pleasure, the source of the pleasures in things outside oneself
the will of all wills: the same ratzon kadum, called by its will, since the taanug is the will inside the will
the hidden Atik: the Keser of Adam Kadmon, where the will is already associated with a thought; covered, but meant to be revealed
the most hidden of all hidden: the beginning of the Kav, which even the thought of Adam Kadmon cannot grasp
the holy Atik: the delight already in chachma, in a particular form; Atik Yomin and Arich Anpin of Atzilus
the bribe: the will makes the intellect biased, so it finds reasons to fit
the short line: one little point of the essence that stands for all of it, the jump from the reshimu to the ratzon kadum
the impression left after the tzimtzum: every possible limited thing, His choices of style without seeing Him in them; still infinite

sections.title: Circles and the straight line: one line that goes down and circles
sections.summary: The chapter sets out to explain the details of the *Kav* as it is in *igulim* (circles). The beginning of the *Kav* goes down a little, circles, goes down and circles again, so that the circles are really one line; in the circles the highest is the best and the innermost the lowest, and in *yosher* (the straight line) it is the other way around.

phrases.en: Now we have to start to understand

phrases.he: בפרטי ענין הקו כמו שהוא בבחינת עגולים כו'.
phrases.en: We have to understand how the *Kav* is already *igulim*

blocks.text: We just finished the *igulim* (circles) and the difference between the *ratzon hamuchlat* (the absolute will) and the *ratzon murkav* (the composite will). **Now we have to start to understand**, "because until now we didn't understand anything": **how the Kav is already igulim.** *Yosher* (the straight line) is really explained only in the next chapter; here he tells you a little about it.

As we explained, *igulim* is like the *ratzon* (will) for a house: the general *ratzon* includes all the particular *ratzonos*, and each one is like a circle. A circle includes everything inside it equally. It is one point that includes everything, like the context: the whole context defines everything.

phrases.he: והנה תחלה יש להקדים בבחינת ראשית הקו הזה
phrases.en: So first we have to explain about the *reshis hakav*

phrases.he: שבא בבחינת אור פנימי ואחר כך מתעגל ונמשך בבחינת אור פנימי וחוזר ומתעגל כו'
phrases.en: first it comes down; the very first *hiyuli Kav* comes down from the *reshimu*, then it circles, and then it goes down and then it circles

blocks.text: **So first we have to explain about the reshis hakav** (the beginning of the line), before the *igulim*. The very first *hiyuli* (raw, general) *Kav* **comes down** from the *reshimu* (the impression left after the *tzimtzum*), **then it circles, and then it goes down and then it circles.**

blocks.title: Drawing it without lifting the pen
blocks.text: It looks like concentric circles with a line going through them, but that is not the way it goes: the circles are made of the line. Draw the same image without picking up your pen. Go down a centimeter, draw a circle back to where you were, go down another centimeter, draw another circle, smaller and smaller. "It's really one line."

phrases.en: and it explains in *Etz Chaim*

phrases.he: שבבחינת עשר ספירות דעגולים, העליון מכולם משובח מכולם והפנימי מכולם גרוע כו',
phrases.en: the best one is on the outside, and the worst one, the lowest *sefira*, is on the inside

phrases.he: ובבחינת עשר ספירות דיושר להיפך, העליון גרוע והפנימי משובח כו'.

blocks.text:
**And it explains in Etz Chaim** that in the ten *sefiros* of *igulim* the highest is the best and the innermost the lowest, and in *yosher* the opposite.

In *igulim*, *Keser* (crown) is outside and *Malchus* (kingship) inside. In *yosher* each *sefira* is *mislabesh* (enclothed) in the one under it: *Keser* in *Chabad*, *Chabad* in the *middos* (emotional attributes), the *middos* in thought, speech and action. So the outermost is *Malchus*, and inside it, in turn, the *middos*, the intellect, the *ratzon* and the *taanug* (delight). Drawn, the difference is whether *Keser* is outside and *Malchus* inside, or the reverse.
Before we talk about circles and things, we have to understand what *igulim* and *yosher* are: "What does a circle mean, and line mean, and you know, what are we talking about?"

sections.title: The ratzon kadum: a hidden first will for yourself that already holds every detail
sections.summary: The *ratzon kadum* (the original will) is revealed compared to the *ratzon hamuchlat*, but it is still hidden, a will for oneself, like the inner stirring to have things your own way before you know it means a house. It is the origin of every detail down to the last blade of grass, and the last deed, the end of the seventh millennium, was first in thought.

phrases.en: the explanation of these matters, these things

phrases.he: הנה ידוע שבחינת רצון קדום זה,
phrases.en: that this first *ratzon*, the *ratzon* for the house in the *mashal*

phrases.he: הגם שלגבי בחינת רצון הפשוט המוחלט בעצמות
phrases.en: even though compared to the *ratzon hamuchlat*
it's already called like a particular revealed *ratzon*
But the truth is, it's really still hidden
it's not revealed at all

phrases.he: כי אינו רק השפעת והמשכת רצון הפשוט של חפץ חסד שהוחלט בעצמות מכבר, כך יהיה בפועל ממש
phrases.en: All you know is that you want your *ratzon hamuchlat* to be revealed *b'poel mamash*

blocks.text: **The explanation of these matters**: **this first ratzon**, the *ratzon* for the house in the *mashal* (analogy), **even though compared to the ratzon hamuchlat, it's already called like a particular revealed ratzon**: you went from just a taste to actually wanting a house. **But the truth is, it's really still hidden; it's not revealed at all.**

With this first *ratzon* you do not yet know what you want. **All you know is that you want your ratzon hamuchlat to be revealed b'poel mamash** (in actual fact). A house you do not want until *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*, and not even really a home, before the *yosher* of *Adam Kadmon*.

blocks.title: Your parents are cramping your style
blocks.text: All you have is an inner stirring, as people have at a certain age: they want to be independent, to have their own space. You do not know what it is; you just feel you do not like the way things are. Your parents are cramping your style: you want to leave the house, your mother says wear a sweater, it's cold, and wash your hands, and it is all in your hair. You just have this *ratzon* to have things the way you want them.

Before that, you do not even know that this means your own house, your own job, your own life, and certainly not what kind of house or where. It is the *ratzon* you have had since you were a little kid: to have something independent that expresses yourself, "this inner desire to like be yourself."

"It doesn't sound right, 'to be yourself,' 'cause you can't not be yourself. It's ridiculous: 'I want to be myself.'" What people mean when they want to be themselves, or find or understand themselves, is that they want to figure out how to get the world to express them, to fit with them.

blocks.title: Getting the world to play your song
blocks.text: Like a guy learning an instrument: he wants to get the world to play his song. He knows what he wants to play even if he does not realize it, because he does not think in terms of music. Certain things sound good to you, like a *ratzon hamuchlat*, but you do not know the song until you bring it out into the instrument: the *hiyuli* that has to come out. So this *ratzon kadum* is still hidden: you know what you want, but not in a tangible way.

phrases.he: ומיד שעולה במחשבה זאת שיהיה הכל,
phrases.en: as soon as it comes up in your thought, I want to do everything that was in my *ratzon hamuchlat*
that's called the first *machshava* and *ratzon*, or the original
which includes everything that's inside of it
all the particular desires inside of it
like we said about the *mashal* of the *ratzon* for a house

blocks.text: **As soon as it comes up in your thought**, "I want to do everything that was in my *ratzon hamuchlat*," **that's called the first machshava and ratzon, or the original**: the *machshava kduma* and *ratzon kadum*.

blocks.title: A father and a firstborn
blocks.text: *Kadum* means original, not first: the origin of everything else, which are branches of it. First just happens to be first. It is the difference between a father and a firstborn. A father you call *kodem*: he precedes his children as their origin. The firstborn just happens to be first.

This original *ratzon* **includes everything that's inside of it, all the particular desires inside of it, like we said about the mashal of the ratzon for a house.** As soon as you say "I want a house," all the other *ratzonos* are included. "The only reason that you want the kitchen sink is because you want a house." They are predicated on the general *ratzon* and included in its definition: your definition of a house includes all those things.

phrases.he: אם כן עדיין רצון קדום זה הכל בעצמו
phrases.en: So, if so, this first *ratzon* is still totally within G-d Himself
it's not revealed yet outside, in anything separate
nevertheless, from it comes everything
afterwards
And this is what it says

phrases.he: כי הוא אמר, במחשבה הקדומה, ויהי כו'
phrases.en: that G-d said, and it was

blocks.text: **So this first ratzon is still totally within G-d Himself.** When a person's *ratzon* for a home first comes up, he is not thinking of anything outside himself; he wants to feel a certain way, to express a certain style, a taste. **It's not revealed yet outside, in anything separate. Nevertheless, from it comes everything afterwards**, because everything is just the expression of that *ratzon*.

**And this is what it says**, "For He said," with the *machshava kduma*, "and it was": **G-d said, and it was.** *Amar* (said) always really means *machshava* (thought). Even when it means speech, it means saying what is on your mind.

blocks.title: A proclamation and a chat with friends
blocks.text: An official proclamation is not just saying what is on your mind: the focus is on the *dibur* (speech), that you are saying it. Talking casually with friends, the focus is on what you are thinking; you say, "Yeah, you know what I mean," because the words do not have to be exact. When you focus on the thought behind the words it is called *amira*; when you focus on the words, *dibur*.

So "For He said, and it was" means He revealed Himself in a way of *machshava*, a *gilui* (revelation) of thought, and here it is the *ratzon kadum*, the original thought. **G-d said**: He said to Himself, He decided how He wanted the world to be, **and it was**: it all came to be according to that. As soon as G-d told Himself, "I want a world, I want a *dira b'tachtonim* (a dwelling below)," everything else follows automatically, as part of making the *dira b'tachtonim*.

phrases.en: And this is called the life of all the worlds
from the beginning of *Adam Kadmon*
until the heel of *Adam Kadmon*
all the way down to the end of *Asiya*

phrases.he: והיינו כל היצור לא נכחד כו'
phrases.en: all of the formed things are not missing from You

phrases.he: שאין פרט היותר אחרון שלא קדם להיות ברצון ובמחשבה זו
phrases.en: There is nothing, not even the smallest detail, that escaped G-d's first *ratzon* and *machshava*; it was all there

blocks.text:
**And this is called the life of all the worlds**: the motivation behind everything is this one point, **from the beginning of Adam Kadmon** (explained next chapter) **until the heel of Adam Kadmon**, a general *partzuf* (stature) that goes **all the way down to the end of Asiya**.

This is what we say, "I think," in *Zichronos* on Rosh Hashana: **all of the formed things are not missing from You.** What does that mean?

**There is nothing, not even the smallest detail, that escaped G-d's first ratzon and machshava**, not the last hair on your head. Did G-d really think about how many hairs are going to be on my head? Yes. That is why everything is *hashgacha pratis* (individual Divine providence), even the way a leaf blows in the tree: G-d knows exactly how many times it will blow back and forth. And it is *noge'a* (relevant) to the whole purpose: for the *dira b'tachtonim* and *Moshiach*, the original *ratzon*, it has to be exactly like that.

blocks.title: The bathroom drapes
blocks.text: "What? Why does that make a difference? That's ridiculous." Think about wanting a house: the whole thing is that you want it exactly the way you want it. Money is no object, and you get down to the nitty-gritty, the bathroom drapes, the decorations. If one of those little things is off, you are living there comfortably, but you do not have the original *ratzon*, that it is your house, your space. That is why a rental where the landlord will not let you change the windows is not a real house.

blocks.title: The bathroom drapes
blocks.text: It is such a little *prat* (detail), but if you cannot do it the way you want, it takes away the whole thing. It could be a good house, but it loses the quality that it is all yours. The bathroom drapes are as important as the general structure. "It's all or nothing deal."

So why does the grass have to blow exactly that way? Because G-d wanted it that way, for whatever reason; that is what made Him feel good. If even one little thing is off, the whole thing is stupid, who needs it? "If a grass won't blow 7,296 times, what's it all worth?" That one blade of grass would ruin everything. So it was all included in this first *ratzon kadum*.

blocks.title: Going out for pizza
blocks.text: "What do you want to do tonight?" "Let's go out for pizza." That has all the details: it is the *ratzon* to open the door. How do you know you want to open the door? "It's all there, don't worry, we got you covered."

phrases.en: On the contrary

phrases.he: סוף מעשה, כמו בסוף אלף הז', עלה במחשבה קדומה זו תחלה
phrases.en: the last thing was really the first in thought

blocks.text: **On the contrary**: the final deed, the end of the seventh millennium, came up first in this *machshava kduma*. The *ratzon* to chew the pizza was the first thought: "So, don't worry, you have the *ratzon* to chew." G-d's main *ratzon* was for the seventh millennium with all its little details, and we are getting closer to it.

"Ah, it's just little details," but these are the main things G-d wanted. Through history it becomes in a way less and in a way more. Adam and Avraham were the big pushers and movers, general people whose stories mean something to all mankind. "Yeah, what about us? The other day I had a story happen to me; why doesn't it get recorded for all times?" They have the advantage of being more general, higher up in the *hishtalshelus* (the chain of descent).

But the main *ratzon* was really for when you go on *mivtzaim* (outreach campaigns) and put *tefillin* on some guy, or learn a *maamar* (discourse). **The last thing was really the first in thought.** For your *ratzon hamuchlat*, the wall structure of your house matters least; most people buy a house and decorate it and furnish it themselves. The big things are just functional. The biggest *gilui* of your *ratzon hamuchlat* is in the little things, where there is no practical reason and it is just how you like it.

So the biggest *gilui* of G-d's *ratzon hamuchlat* is in "the stupid little things," that He wants the world for *Moshiach* *davka* (precisely) this way. "He could have done it in another way." "Yeah, but He likes it this way." Why are trees green? Why aren't the leaves brown and the trunks green? "Why does there have to be a bird-dropping spider? Nobody knows why." And there is room to say more about it.

sections.title: In the language of the Zohar: Atika d'Atikin, Atika Stima'a and Atika Kadisha
sections.summary: A parenthesis puts the *ratzon kadum* into the *Zohar*'s terms. In the *ratzon* there is a *taanug*, and they are one: as the source of all the pleasures and wills to come, in the *Kav* after the *tzimtzum*, it is *Atika d'Atikin*, the pleasure of all pleasures; enclothed in the *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon*, already associated with a thought, it is *Atika Stima'a*, hidden but meant to be revealed; and as the pleasure already in a particular form, in *Atzilus*, it is *Atika Kadisha*.

phrases.en: in the words of the *Zohar*
the *ratzon kadum* is called the *Atik* of all *Atiks*, the inner pleasure behind all pleasure
or the hidden *Atik*

phrases.he: והוא בחינת רעוא דכל רעווין עילאין
phrases.en: This is also the *ratzon* of all upper *ratzonos*, the inner *ratzon*
which is revealed on the forehead of *Atika Kadisha*
because the *ratzon* inside the *ratzon* is the *taanug*
And they're really one thing

blocks.text: **In the words of the Zohar**: "Now we're going to do this kabbalistic parentheses to put everything in context for you. Since you're used to learning things in Zoharatic terminology, we're going to now help you translate it into your mother tongue, all right? Ready for this?"

In the *Zohar*'s language **the ratzon kadum is called the Atik of all Atiks**, *Atika d'Atikin*, the inner pleasure behind all pleasure, **or the hidden Atik**, *Atika Stima'a*; the difference between them comes at the end of the parenthesis. **This is also the ratzon of all upper ratzonos**, *ra'ava d'chol ra'avin*: both the inner *taanug* and the inner *ratzon*, **revealed on the forehead of Atika Kadisha**, the *taanug* revealed in something particular.

Why both *Atika d'Atikin* and *ra'ava d'chol ra'avin*? **Because the ratzon inside the ratzon is the taanug. And they're really one thing**: the *ratzon*, the *ratzon kadum*, the *taanug*, "you can call them whatever you want to call it."

phrases.he: וברצון הפשוט ההיולי שבחפץ חסד ההיולי (הנזכר לעיל באות יוד ואות יא) היה כלול בו התענוג
phrases.en: Even in the *hiyuli ratzon pashut* there was enclosed the *hiyuli taanug pashut*

phrases.he: הפשוט שבעצמות שנקרא שעשועי המלך בעצמותו כו'

phrases.en: in each of the three levels there's a *ratzon* and there's also the *taanug*
until it comes to a *prat*
that I'm going to be king

phrases.he: שזה בחינת מלכות דאין סוף שלפני הצמצום
phrases.en: which is the *Malchus d'Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*, which is the *ratzon hamuchlat* for our world

phrases.he: הכל בחינת שעשועי המלך בעצמו בטהירו עילאה
phrases.en: Those are all G-d's essential *taanug* in Himself

blocks.text: **Even in the hiyuli ratzon pashut**, the will of the *hiyuli chafetz chesed* (the desire for kindness) of chapters 10 and 11, **there was enclosed the hiyuli taanug pashut**. And **in each of the three levels there's a ratzon and there's also the taanug, until it comes to a prat**, *Ana Emloch*, **that I'm going to be king**, the *ratzon hamuchlat* for our world. **Those are all G-d's essential taanug in Himself**: the *taanug* side, the pleasure G-d has in Himself.

phrases.en: but once you talk about *Atika d'Atikin*
which is the source of all pleasures, meaning pleasures you have in things separate from yourself
or the *ratzon* of all *ratzonos*
that's in the *Kav* that's after the *tzimtzum*
which is like one general *ratzon* or one general *taanug*, that you want to express yourself
that are going to come out *b'gilui*

blocks.text: **But once you talk about Atika d'Atikin, which is the source of all pleasures**, pleasures in things separate from yourself, it is **in the Kav that's after the tzimtzum**, **one general ratzon or one general taanug, that you want to express yourself.** It is the intermediary: before it, all enjoyment and *ratzon* is for yourself; after it, in things outside yourself. So it is the pleasure of all pleasures and the *ratzon* of all *ratzonos* **that are going to come out b'gilui** (in revelation).

phrases.he: ועתיקא סתימאה הוא בבחינת כתר דאדם קדמון
phrases.en: when we say *Atika Stima'a*, that is the *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon*

phrases.he: שהוא בהעלם הרצון והתענוג לעצמו עדיין,
phrases.en: This is still the hidden *ratzon* and pleasure which is for yourself

is called totally hidden

phrases.en: that even the *machshava* of *Adam Kadmon* cannot *tofes* it
that He wants to actually have it: to have the revealed *ratzon* and *taanug* for the *sefiros* of *Atzilus*, and the revealed *ratzon* and *taanug* for *Beriya* and for *Yetzira* and *Asiya* also

blocks.text: **When we say Atika Stima'a, that is the Keser of Adam Kadmon.** *Stima'a*, hidden, always means where it is associated with a *machshava*, like the *machshava stima'a* and *mocha stima'a* discussed later: the way it is in *Keser*, but already come into a *machshava* and associated with something, which is a thing of *bina* (understanding).

blocks.text: That is like the *yosher* of *Adam Kadmon*, the world of *Beriya*, connected with *machshava*. As the *igul* above it, it is *Atika d'Atikin*; *mislabesh* in the *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon*, it is *Atika Stima'a*, hidden within. The general *ratzon* to express yourself already motivates particular *ratzonos*, but the hidden *ratzon* behind them is still just to reveal your *ratzon hamuchlat*.

blocks.text: **This is still the hidden ratzon and pleasure which is for yourself, just that you want that you should now be revealed.** You do not really want the house; you want to feel a certain way, and now you want it actually to happen, not just to have it in your *ratzon hamuchlat*. The *ratzon hamuchlat* just means, "Yeah, in theory I like things that way, but right now I'm not interested."

blocks.title: Your favorite ice cream
blocks.text: What is your favorite flavor of ice cream? Your favorite song, your favorite style of music? That does not mean you are in the mood to eat it or listen to it right now. It is just in theory: "Yeah, okay, that's what."

blocks.title: Interviewing G-d
blocks.text: Say they interview G-d: "G-d, if You were going to make a world, how would You like it? Would You like being king of a universe?" "Yeah, I would really love being king of a universe, and I would want it like this and like that." G-d was daydreaming about what it would be like, but He did not actually want to do it.

Right then He was busy "playing with His train set." It's not *kavod* (dignified)? Playing chess? "Why G-d has to be like this sophisticated guy? He could be playing a little kid, why not?" In this *hishtalshelus* He reveals Himself in big things, like a king; in another He could do little things. "G-d doesn't have any parents to tell Him what to do. They can't tell Him not to play with the trains, it's not *kavod*."

sensitivity.reason: A playful picture of G-d playing with a train set and chess, with no parents to tell Him it is undignified; a reader may take it as irreverent.
sensitivity.publishable: It would not be *kavod* (dignified) in this *hishtalshelus*, where He is the King and decided to reveal Himself in big things, in a dignified way. In another *hishtalshelus* He could reveal Himself in little things. Nothing outside Him tells Him what is fitting.

blocks.text: So **that there should be a revealed ratzon and taanug to bring out the ten sefiros**: **that's why it's called the hidden taanug**, *Atika Stima'a*, hidden in relation to being revealed: **it's just like covered, but you know it's really there**, meant to be revealed.

**But the beginning of the Kav is called totally hidden**, *stima d'chol stimin*, **that even the machshava of Adam Kadmon cannot tofes** (grasp) **it**, while *Atika Stima'a* is the *taanug* already *mislabesh* in that *machshava*. *Stima* is always the thought of the *ratzon*, not of the intellect: like association, when you learn a language and just know, before thinking, that this idea goes with that sound.
So it is still hidden; only He thought **that He wants to actually have it: to have the revealed ratzon and taanug for the sefiros of Atzilus**, and for *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya* also.

phrases.en: *Atika Kadisha*, though, is the *taanug* that is in the *chachma* already

phrases.he: והוא בחינת עתיק יומין ואריך אנפין דאצילות,
phrases.en: the *taanug* and the *ratzon* of *Atzilus*
that's already a revealed *ratzon*
like we'll explain everything in detail

blocks.text:
**Atika Kadisha, though, is the taanug that is in the chachma already**: a delight already coming in a particular form. It is *Atik Yomin* and *Arich Anpin* of *Atzilus*, **the taanug and the ratzon of Atzilus**: **that's already a revealed ratzon.**

The original *ratzon*, *Atika d'Atikin*, is the inner delight of yourself. Going through *Adam Kadmon* it becomes associated with a form, and you delight that it be *davka* this form, because once you chose it, it will reveal you. That is *Atika Kadisha*: holy, but already connected. **We'll explain everything in detail.**

So far: even the *ratzon kadum*, the first *gilui* after the *Kav*, is still hidden, still only for yourself. The *igulim* until *yosher* are all for yourself; you have not thought about the world yet. You know you want to reveal something in the world, but have not figured out what that means. It is the *ratzon* for a home before it becomes a *ratzon* for a house: you do not want a building yet, you just want to feel at home.

Sometimes people have these desires and do not know what they are, especially Jewish people, "but even *goyim* also": they feel they are not using their potential, their life is empty, they are missing something. They know they want to feel fulfilled, but not what will give it to them, because the *ratzon* is still *b'helem* (hidden). Until they figure it out, it can motivate them to try all kinds of weird things.

sensitivity.reason: Uses the word goyim for non-Jews, which many readers take as dismissive.
sensitivity.publishable: Sometimes people have these desires and do not know what they are, especially Jewish people, but non-Jews also: they feel they are not using their potential, their life is empty, they are missing something. They know they want to feel fulfilled, but not what will give it to them, because the *ratzon* is still *b'helem* (hidden). Until they figure it out, it can motivate them to try all kinds of weird things.

blocks.text: It is very *b'gilui* at a certain age. Teenagers think they want to be a successful businessman, or married with a house; when that doesn't do it, they have a midlife crisis: "Maybe I should have got that red convertible I always wanted, instead of being responsible and saving all my money for a house." So they buy the hot rod, dress like a teenager and act stupid. Then they get into Eastern religions or something. "And yeah, if they're lucky, they find Rabbi Markel's website, and then life becomes good again."

sensitivity.reason: Lumps Eastern religions in with a midlife crisis's foolishness, and names Rabbi Markel's website as the happy ending, a joke about a living teacher printed under Rabbi Walters' name.
sensitivity.publishable: It is very *b'gilui* at a certain age. Teenagers think they want to be a successful businessman, or married with a house; when that doesn't do it, they have a midlife crisis: "Maybe I should have got that red convertible I always wanted, instead of being responsible and saving all my money for a house." So they buy the hot rod, dress like a teenager and act stupid, and then try something else, until, if they are lucky, they find Chassidus, and life becomes good again.

blocks.text: Every person, even one who is not Jewish, as a person has the inner desire to know G-d, to know the truth, especially G-dliness. A Jew is unique in wanting a connection higher than intellect, to have *mesirus nefesh* (self-sacrifice) for G-d. But being a person means wanting to know G-dliness. "So everybody wants to learn Chassidus."

So they try all kinds of things that give them little tastes, "the dripping of this liquid into their brain," but it is not the pure stuff. Like someone used to "government grade" drugs who gets cheap stuff laced with rat poison. "I never tried either one, so I don't know the difference. But it sounds like it's pretty bad."

sensitivity.reason: A joke comparing other spiritual paths to cheap street drugs laced with rat poison, against pure "government grade" drugs.

sections.title: Circles: each cause surrounds its effect, and the effect never reaches it
sections.summary: The ten *sefiros* of *igulim* are a wheel inside a wheel: every cause surrounds its effect, and the effect reaches it only from far away, as the reasons a kid makes up never capture why he wants a bike. Each circle starts as one undivided point, a bias, down to the *sof maaseh*, the final deed, which in the circles is the flimsiest and innermost; so too the *ratzon kadum* is ten circles, from the will for a *dira b'tachtonim* to the will for this exact world.

phrases.he: והנה בחינת עשר ספירות דעגולים זה תחת זה הוא כידוע,
phrases.en: the ten *sefiros* of *igulim*, one under the other
that every cause surrounds its effect
And the effect does not grasp, it doesn't reach its cause
only in a very far away, very far from it
like a wheel inside of a wheel

blocks.text: **The ten sefiros of igulim, one under the other**: what does it mean that they are like a circle inside a circle? As is known, **every cause surrounds its effect. And the effect does not grasp, it doesn't reach its cause**, its source, except **only in a very far away, very far from it, like a wheel inside of a wheel.**

blocks.title: A wheel inside a wheel
blocks.text: A wheel inside a wheel: there is the inner source, the real thing you want, like the inner desire for the house, and the lower thing that comes out of it, the way you are going to get it. That will never fully give you what you want; it really stays higher.

The quote is from Ezekiel's vision of the Divine chariot: the *Ofanim* (a class of angels) look like a wheel inside a wheel, with eyes all over them. What we mean is concentric circles, a circle inside a circle.

blocks.title: Ripples in a pond
blocks.text: Concentric circles: a big circle and smaller ones inside it around the same center, like ripples in a pond. Except that here it goes from the outside in: first the outer circle, then the inner one, and the inner one. It is not like a pebble dropped in a pond, starting from the middle. Though even there the biggest ripple goes out first, and smaller and smaller ones fill in inside it as it grows.

In the Ramak's *hishtalshelus*, which speaks of it from the *reshimu*, the *igulim* do start from the middle and come out. But we are talking about the Arizal's *hishtalshelus*, already set up with the light going through it, so it comes from the top of the circle and goes in.

blocks.text: **We're going to understand this from the revealed ratzon**: the *mashal* he gives now is what he explains about the *ratzonos* of *Atzilus* in chapters 20 and 21.

**Even though the ratzon includes ten**, **it has intellect and emotions**: the *chachma* (wisdom) is the inner goal, and the emotions follow, this is good and this is bad. But **it starts off just as one thing; you don't see any divisions in it yet. This is called the circle of a general ratzon**, encompassing all inside it, **which comes specifically from its force**, **but it comes in a far-off way.**

which is called its effect

as is known
and it will never reach it

blocks.text: **Like the reason and the intellect for the ratzon, which is called its effect: it's impossible for it to be close to its source, its cause, which is the desire**, because there is no reason for a *ratzon* at all, **as is known.**

blocks.title: A kid who wants a bike
blocks.text: A kid wants a bike. That is it, *nekuda* (period), as they say in Hebrew. At this level there is no reason; he wants it because he wants it. Once he decides, he makes up reasons, excuses to tell his parents: "Oh, I can get to school faster, and it's healthy." Those reasons are invented because of his *ratzon*; they do not make it. His *ratzon* is the cause, and they are its effect.

blocks.title: A kid who wants a bike
blocks.text: And they do not capture the *ratzon*, so they are not the real reason. "You don't need the bike to get to school, you can walk." "But I need to be there on time." "Also you can run. That way you get the exercise, and you get there on time. We'll jog there every day."

blocks.title: Helping shlep the couch
blocks.text: People often do not want to say directly what they want, so they give a side reason, to make it look like a rule when there is no rule, just what they want. "Can you help me *shlep* my couch?" "Oh, I really would love to, but..." They just don't want to, so they find an excuse. The advantage of a reason is that it takes it off yourself: "It's not that I don't want to; something else is making me not able to."

blocks.title: Helping shlep the couch
blocks.text: But then you are susceptible to being put in a corner, because they can disprove your reason: "Oh, it's so perfect, I'll have somebody take care of the thing you had to do, and you can help me." "Oh, no, now look what I got myself into." The reason never really captures the *ratzon*.

blocks.title: A belief and its proofs
blocks.text:
The same with a belief. Say people believe the Rebbe is *Moshiach*. "Why do you believe?" "This *sicha* (talk), this Rambam, this whatever." It does not mean it is not true, but they believe it because they believe it, not because of the proofs. Disprove them and they will not say, "All right, you're right, never mind"; they will find another, because the intellect comes from the *ratzon*.

That is *chachma* to *bina*: the *igul* (circle) of the *chachma* forces the *igul* of the *bina* to prove it, but the proofs never capture the *chachma*. And the inner *ratzon* is for the Rebbe: they want the Rebbe to be *Moshiach*.

sensitivity.reason: Uses those in Chabad who hold that the Rebbe is Moshiach as the example of a belief held regardless of proof, a live and divisive question within the movement.
sensitivity.publishable:
The same with a belief. "Why do you believe?" "Oh, this source, this proof, this whatever." It does not mean it is not true, but people believe it because they believe it, not because of the proofs. Disprove them and they will not say, "All right, you're right, never mind"; they will find another, because the intellect comes from the *ratzon*.

That is *chachma* to *bina*: the *igul* (circle) of the *chachma* forces the *igul* of the *bina* to prove it, but the proofs never capture the *chachma*, and behind it is the inner *ratzon*.

blocks.text: Again: **it's impossible for it to be close to its source, its cause**, the *ratzon*, because **there's no reason for ratzon whatsoever**, **and it will never reach it.** The intellect never really captures the *ratzon*.

blocks.text: **Nevertheless, the chachma is coming from the ratzon**, and it too is **without a recognizable division into ten**: just a *nekuda* (point), like a bias. Your *ratzon* does not give you a particular *chachma*; it biases your *sechel* (intellect) to lean a certain way, so whenever you come to a particular reasoning, it finds something that fits.

blocks.title: A bias toward kindness
blocks.text: Say you have a *ratzon* toward *chesed* (kindness). Your intellect leans toward *chesed*, so you will be liberal-minded, whether just toward your son, that you always look at him favorably, or in general, liberal or conservative, politically or in anything. It is a leaning, not yet a particular reasoning: you look for reasoning and a worldview that fit how you want things to turn out. Yet the *sechel* never captures the *ratzon*; it is just a way to get it to come out.

**This is like a bribe** (*shochad*): **the bribe makes you find the reason for the ratzon.** Someone bribed you over a court case: you have no reason yet why he should be innocent, but now you will always look at things with that bias.

**And even though this reason also includes ten**, *ratzon*, *sechel* and *middos*, a whole world of coming up with a reason and proving it, it comes as a general thing: **right now you didn't develop and reveal all those pratim** (details); **right now it's just the point, the bias.**

phrases.he: ועל דרך זה לא ישיגנו העיגול דבינה שנעשה מכחו,
phrases.en: and so too the *bina* doesn't reach the *chachma*

phrases.he: ועל דרך זה המדות זה תחת זה עד סוף מעשה
phrases.en: and so too with each emotion, one after the other, until it comes to *sof maaseh*
which is the last thing

phrases.he: והכל ברצונו לעצמו כלול הכל עד סוף מעשה
phrases.en: and all this is all in the desire for himself, which includes everything, till the final action
which is the innermost thing of everything

blocks.text: **And so too the bina doesn't reach the chachma.** The claim, the view, the belief is the *chachma*; the proofs you bring for it are the *bina*; and they do not meet. The proofs do not really prove it, and they cannot really change it.
You see this more openly in alternative stuff: pseudo-sciences, New Age spirituality, "cultish-type things." There is very little reasoning; they bring one little proof and pile everything on it.

sensitivity.reason: A dismissive remark about New Age spirituality, pseudo-sciences and "cultish-type things".
sensitivity.publishable: You see this more openly where a view has very little reasoning behind it: they bring one little proof and pile everything on it.

blocks.text: **And so too with each emotion, one after the other**: it comes out that a thing is good and you should like it, **until it comes to sof maaseh** (the final action), **which is the last thing**, in a way the most fake and the most flimsy.

It is not even an actual thing, a total daydream of things being a certain way; it is not really going to happen, and it will never give you what you want. By the time you get down to action, you cannot get your inner desire, to be rich, or a house, even a home, to express your taste. It is such little things that in a way it does not capture what you want at all.

blocks.title: A kid in a bakery with two bucks
blocks.text: It is such a limited self-expression. That is why kids in a bakery or a store have trouble deciding: in your imagination you have so many things you want, and all you have is two bucks. Even with enough money for any one thing, you can walk away with only one. In life too you can only do one thing, and it has to express all your emotions, your taste and your whole worldview and inner desire, "and you know, it's like nothing."

**And all this is all in the desire for himself, which includes everything, till the final action.** Even the last *igul* is not the *pratim* of how he will do it, only the bias, the *nekuda*: "Oh, I decide, I'm doing this." He has not figured out how, **which is the innermost thing of everything.**

phrases.he: וכך הוא ברצון הנעלם הנקרא רצון הקדום הנזכר לעיל, מקור כל הרצונות

and it includes ten *sefiros*
so too the first *ratzon* that G-d had for the whole world is like this

phrases.he: עיגול בתוך עיגול עד עיגול דסוף מעשה,
phrases.en: in a way of a circle inside of a circle, until the circle of the *sof maaseh*
this is the *ratzon* for *sof maaseh*

phrases.he: להיות כל אשר חפץ עושה בפועל ממש כו'
phrases.en: that *Hashem* wanted to actually do everything that He wanted, to actually make the world
the first circle that includes everything

blocks.text: So it is in the hidden will, surrounded by all the other *igulim*. The biggest thing is the inner *ratzon*: say you want the house, the home. That makes a *chachma*, a certain picture. Then a *bina* justifies and explains it and makes distinctions: what brings it closer to what you want and what makes it farther. Once you divide it into parts, you can have *middos*.

blocks.question: Why can't you have middos from a chachma?
blocks.text: Because in *chachma* it is all or nothing: it is or it is not. So how can you like it, like it more, like it less? Once you have *middos* from *bina*, you recognize that there are a bunch of parts, and you can be excited that it is getting closer.

You like this a little more, that a little less; you work on it and slowly build it the way you want. The *middos* are how you react, change and measure things out. Making a house, you decide how big the kitchen and the other rooms are: the *middos*, even the physical dimensions, come from an understanding in *bina* of the picture in *chachma* of what you want in *Keser*.

You want to express your taste. Once you have a picture of what expresses it, you figure out its parts, draw plans and work out the details. The details come out in the *middos*, and the *middos* in the *sof maaseh*, where you actually do something: you buy a house.

You could design more than one house that fits your *middos*, and you pick one: "Why this one?" "I want that one." That too is a *nekuda*: you make up your mind, and now it expresses your inner *ratzon*. So it is the innermost, existing only in the context of the rest: you want this house for these *middos*, and care about them only within this *bina* and *chachma*.

blocks.title: Dressing in style
blocks.text: A person wants to dress in style. They buy a certain thing. Why? Because it has certain shapes and colors, which are *middos*. Why care about those? Because in *bina* they associate them with being in style. The *chachma* is their picture of what being in style means, different for different groups. The inner *ratzon* is the desire to be in style, or to express themselves, depending how far in you go. So the thing exists only within the context of all that surrounds it: that is why it is called the *pnimi* (innermost).

**This is the ratzon hane'elam, which is called the ratzon kadum, the source of all the ratzonos, and it includes ten sefiros.** **So too** G-d's first *ratzon* for the whole world: one general circle that includes all ten, **in a way of a circle inside of a circle, until the circle of the sof maaseh.**

First the *ratzon* for a *dira b'tachtonim*, the most general. Then that it have a certain form, the inner thing of *Atzilus*; then that the form be associated with certain things; then certain *middos*; until a certain *sof maaseh*, the final *igul*: that G-d wants this world exactly the way it is. Because on the level of the *middos* there could still be infinite worlds that meet those specifications.

And **the first circle that includes everything**, is the *ratzon kadum*. Everything exists only within its context: the only reason G-d wants anything, at least as He set up the *hishtalshelus*, is that it is part of the *dira b'tachtonim*. "That's it." Nothing has meaning without it, and nothing alone ever reaches it. So the *gilui* in *Atzilus* does not really express it; He chose that it go through that, but it does not fully capture it.

blocks.title: Giving flowers
blocks.text: You have to read between the lines; nothing captures it. Like giving flowers: it does not express anything, it is such a little thing. The *etzem* (essence) stays a *makif* (encompassing light) over it and does not come into any *kli* (vessel). You see from the context that you are using it to express that thing, but it is just a sign, a token.

blocks.title: The strings of the tallis
blocks.text: That is the idea of *tzitzis*. The *tallis* represents a big *makif* that goes around everything, and to express it to the next level you need strings that come out, a token representation of it.

**Until the circle of the sof maaseh**, the *ratzon* for the final deed: **that Hashem wanted to actually do everything that He wanted, to actually make the world.** And **the first circle that includes everything**, is the *ratzon kadum* mentioned above.

So it works with the *igulim*: first the *ratzon kadum*, the original desire for the *dira b'tachtonim*, the seventh millennium. It goes down from that general desire to the *ratzon* for the exact form of the world, down to every last hair on your head. Once that picture, the whole of history, was decided, G-d decided to do it *b'poel mamash*. That is the last circle.

sections.title: Yosher: once you decide to do it, the order turns over and the deed is on top
sections.summary: When the will for oneself comes to be done in actual fact, everything reverses: the *ratzon* hides in the intellect, the intellect in the *middos*, and the *middos* in the deed, until the *sof maaseh*, which in the circles was a daydream, becomes the king that everything must fit. *Igulim* are the dream and the passion, *teshuva*; *yosher* is the practical, the good deeds, where the bottom line is whether you do it.

phrases.he: וכשבא הרצון לעצמו הזה להיות בפועל ממש
phrases.en: and when this *ratzon* for Himself comes, that He actually wants to do it
it's the opposite

blocks.title: Dreaming of a home
blocks.text: **And when this ratzon for Himself comes, that He actually wants to do it**, it is the opposite. Say a guy wants a home: "Oh, I'd really like to have my own space." He dreams about his dream house, what he thinks is cool, makes a whole picture, even looks at particular houses, but "he's thinking of doing it, but it's not really thinking of doing it"; he is not serious. Then comes a point when he has figured out clearly enough what he wants and decides to actually do it, and his whole perspective changes: he has to stop dreaming and start doing.

His focus becomes the opposite. Until now the main thing was what he wants, so everything had to be transparent to that; he could choose anything, as they tell kids, "You can be whatever you want to be." In *igulim*, the biggest thing, which surrounds and defines everything, is what you want. When you actually want to do it, you have to change your focus.

blocks.title: The Frierdiker Rebbe's plan on the boat
blocks.text: On the boat to America the Frierdiker Rebbe (the Previous Rebbe) dictated to his secretary his plan for America: *Merkos L'Inyonei Chinuch*, *Kehos* and *Machane Israel*. Why not wait until he got there and evaluate the situation? "Because I don't want to come there and already be influenced by what I see, and then my plan will be an American Judaism. I want to have a European Judaism, an uncompromised ideal of the way things should be."

There are always two steps. First you make a goal, and in deciding it you should not consider the outside world: if everything went just as you dream, what is your ideal? There the top circle has to be what you want, what would really make you happy, and everything else has to be flexible, transparent to it.

blocks.title: I need a million dollars? I'll get a job
blocks.text: Then, when you decide actually to do it, the thing you picked from the dream becomes your top priority, and everything has to fit within it. It has to look exactly like that; it is not compromisable. "Well, that's going to be hard." "I don't care if it's going to be hard. What do I have to do to do it?" "It's going to cost you a lot of money." "I need a million dollars? Okay, I'll get a job then." Or a loan, or ask my parents. You figure out how.

So when you do it *b'poel mamash*, everything is defined the opposite way. The *sof maaseh* becomes the king of everything, totally not flexible, and it defines everything else. That is the difference between *igulim* and *yosher*: when you actually want to do it, that is the ten *sefiros* of *yosher*, and there the *maaseh* (deed) is at the top.

blocks.title: Getting the pizza
blocks.text: "What are you in the mood to do tonight?" You think only of what you would really like if everything went perfectly, not whether there is a way to do it. You'd like pizza. So you make a firm commitment: "Okay, that's it, I'm going to do it." Now you figure it out: get dressed, find wheels, scrape around for cash. Or if that doesn't work, make it yourself. If you really want it, you will find a way. *Ein davar ha'omed bifnei haratzon*: nothing stands in the way of the will.

The same with G-d. He planned the *dira b'tachtonim* in *igulim*, where everything was transparent to His *ratzon*. Once He figured out a certain form, a certain *maaseh*, and decided He wants it *b'poel mamash*, that becomes the top thing, and everything in the *hishtalshelus* from then on follows that *sof maaseh*. It becomes the *Keser*: the *Malchus* of the higher one becomes the *Keser* of the lower one, the king. If the king tells you, "I want you to move this mountain," you cannot tell him no. "And it's going to happen."

blocks.question: Is this the change from igulim to yosher, or from yosher to igulim?
blocks.text: You can go either way, but here we are going from *igulim* to *yosher*. We just finished the ten *sefiros* of *igulim*, and now the *Malchus* of *igulim* becomes the top thing, totally set.

But it is not an ordinary *Malchus* of the higher becoming *Keser* of the lower; it is not the same *Malchus*. Your main *ratzon* now is that it actually happen, and you still have to figure out what the house will look like. Your focus is on the physical building, not on the planning and the *ratzon* for it. That *ratzon* for the house is only there to motivate you to get it, because you do not really care about the house; you want the home.

There are two *ratzonos*. The *ratzon* of *yosher* is the lowest; you do not care about it. The *ratzon* of *igulim* is the highest: that you get the pleasure you want. The pleasure of getting the building is a low means to an end, to get you to make the house. "It's just like a candy, it's a bait."

Whether you enjoy house shopping is what you care about least, and people usually do not enjoy it much: it is the flimsiest *ratzon* and *taanug*, created only enough to get you to do it. The intellect counts a little more, because you need it to do it right; the *middos* more, that you feel good about it; and the main thing is that you actually have the house.

We just finished the *sefiros* of *igulim*, where the top one is the main one and the inside one the least important. Because there you focus on what you want, and whatever represents it is a token that does not reach what it represents, so it is transparent, kind of irrelevant. If you are making a language and naming something, the name is irrelevant; you can pick any name. The main thing is you, what you decide.

The whole purpose of Elul, Rosh Hashana and Yom Kippur is to recognize the *sefiros* of *igulim*, up to the top *igul*: to have *mesirus nefesh* for G-d Himself, the *Baal HaRatzon* (the One whose will it is). If He told us to chop wood, we would chop wood; "if He tells us to jump off the roof, we'll jump off the roof"; to run around waving our hands and screaming like an insane person, we'll do that. If He wants eleven *sefiros*, there will be eleven. Nature, order, the *dira b'tachtonim* and *gilui Atzmus* are all invented by Him, and really irrelevant.

So to do *teshuva* (return) you have to say, "I don't care about Shabbos, I don't care about *aveira* (sin), I don't care about Torah and *mitzvos* at all; just whatever G-d wants me to do." Not as things that have something to them on their own, "and this whole *dira b'tachtonim* thing, we don't care about that either." That is *teshuva*: reconnecting to the original source, the first *igul*.

blocks.text: From Yom Kippur to Sukkos is going into *yosher*, where it is the opposite. Once you commit that whatever G-d wants you will do, the thing He picks takes on the full force of your *mesirus nefesh*. If He says to put on *tefillin* every day, you will die to put on *tefillin* every day. Communist Russia could not stop them from *tefillin* or Shabbos, even down to shoelaces: if somebody tells you to tie them the way the *goyim* do, "you'll laugh in their face and let them kill you." Even for the smallest *prat* of the *ratzon*, total *mesirus nefesh*.

blocks.text: But to get there you first have to stop caring about the things themselves: that is the *igulim*, where the main thing is only His *ratzon*. Then, when G-d chooses how He wants it *b'poel mamash*, it switches to *yosher*, and the main thing becomes the *maaseh*, done exactly according to the outward side, the *pratim* of *halacha*. The *kavanos* (intentions) are irrelevant, just ways to get you there. "The main thing is not your *kavana* and your feelings and all that holy stuff, the main thing is that you do it."

blocks.text: Like the story last week of the Frierdiker Rebbe coming to America, and the *shliach* (emissary) going to Johannesburg, "I think." Making your plan in 770 or on the boat is *igulim*: you plan by what you want, not by what is possible and practical, and everything else is *batel* (nullified) to that. Once you choose one plan *b'poel mamash*, it is totally set, and everything is figuring out how to get there, even how to get yourself to want it. That is a *hachlata* (a decision): you switch, and the main thing becomes the *maaseh*.

blocks.title: A kid in a toy store with a dollar
blocks.text: While planning which house you want, you are flexible: this one, that one. Eventually you have to say, "That's it. I'm going to do only one," and it is hard for people to make that jump: "It's an immaturity." Kids in a toy store with a dollar want everything, so whatever they finally get is disappointing, because it is not everything else. But you have to pick one and not change your goal: "every time you change your goal, you start over." Make a firm resolution to do it no matter what, and then everything is figuring out how.

blocks.text:
That is why on Sukkos you go into the *sukka*: the *mitzvos* are like a temporary structure. You have to see through it, that you do them only because G-d said so, the *makif* of the *igulim* in the *yosher*. That is why it is temporary, and why you see through the roof.

"So I like to tell people on Sukkos that the purpose of Sukkos is to teach us that you're not supposed to be *frum* (religious)." People get a picture of what being *frum* means, make that their goal and forget that they just want to do whatever G-d wants. All year you have a house, a set structure like a *Shulchan Aruch*, your picture of how you are supposed to be, protected from outside influences. Every now and then you have to go out of your box, do *teshuva* and remember why you do it, that it is flexible. Then you make it set again: most of the year it has to be a house.

blocks.text: But you have to at least start with the *kavana* that it is *lishma* (for its own sake). That is why in *halacha* the main thing is to remember *lishma* when you start: that is when you decide, and you have to decide because G-d said so. Once you decide, you can forget why; it is now a different *ratzon*, focused on how to do it. You do not have to hold the *kavana* the whole time.

blocks.text: In *igulim* the focus is on yourself: you want the house because it will make you happy, fulfilled, with your own space. But once this *ratzon* for yourself is to be *b'poel mamash*, once you decide actually to do a certain house, **it's the opposite.**

phrases.en: the *ratzon* becomes hidden
and it goes into *sechel*
and the *sechel* surrounds the *ratzon*, meaning that it's bigger than the *ratzon*

phrases.he: והשכל מתעלם ומתלבש במדות זה תחת זה
phrases.en: then the *sechel* gets hidden and gets put into the *middos*, one under the other

phrases.he: עד סוף מעשה, הוא העליון מהכל
phrases.en: until the *sof maaseh* goes on top of everything, the highest one of everything

blocks.text: **The ratzon becomes hidden, and it goes into sechel.** "Okay, that's it, I want to actually get a house." You put the *ratzon* aside: the main thing now is not my *ratzon* but the *sechel*, which has to tell me what is reasonable to want.

blocks.title: Buckingham Palace for the garage
blocks.text: In *igulim* you say, "I would like to live in a great big palace, maybe Buckingham Palace, or maybe we'll use Buckingham Palace for the garage and build a bigger palace." Then he comes to do it, reaches into his pocket and finds two nickels and a dime: enough for a cardboard box outside the museum. His intellect tells him to drop his expectations a little, or get a job, or come up with something more reasonable, and figure out a way to do it.

Even if he does not lower his desire, in a way he does, because in the *sechel* his picture becomes something practical and limited. The way of the *oros d'Tohu* (lights of Chaos) with the *kelim d'Tikun* (vessels of Repair) is not to lower your final goal but to find a practical way that starts leading toward it. Normally, though, people just do *oros d'Tikun* with *kelim d'Tikun*. We are not up to *Tikun* yet, but for now it is almost the same thing.

So the *sechel* becomes the main thing: **and the sechel surrounds the ratzon, meaning that it's bigger than the ratzon**, and the *ratzon* does not reach it. "What you want is very nice, but if it doesn't make sense, that's too bad." The *sechel* is more real now: it can change the *ratzon*, but the *ratzon* cannot change the *sechel*. The *sechel* is on top.

**Then the sechel gets hidden and gets put into the middos, one under the other.** It sounds very good on paper, but the *middos* kick in and tell the *sechel* which plan you will do: "I know in theory I could do that, but I'm sorry, I'm scared, I'm not going to do it." Or, "I don't like doing it." "You can make a lot of money being a garbage man, it has good benefits." "Yeah, I don't want to do that."

blocks.question: Are the middos the same ratzon?
blocks.text: No. *Middos* means the way you relate to something, the way you react. There is a *ratzon* higher than *sechel* and a *ratzon* lower than *sechel*, and the one lower than *sechel* is in the *middos*.

blocks.title: I like candy
blocks.text: I like candy: that is my *ratzon*, higher than *sechel*. My *sechel* tells me what will get me candy: if I behave, I get candy. The *middos* are how I react when, say, my parents are watching and I can listen or not. "*Ratzon* plus *sechel* equals *midda*": it is a function, and the *sechel* spins out which *midda* you should have. That you now see listening to your parents as good, with a *chesed* toward it, and are scared to cross them because then they won't give you the candy: those are *middos*. Your inner desire is for the candy.

Before, the *sechel* was the bigger circle with the *middos* inside it. Now the *sechel* is *metzamtzem* (contracted) and the *middos* go around it; then the *middos* are *metzamtzem* and the *maaseh* goes around them, **the middos one under the other, until the sof maaseh goes on top of everything, the highest one of everything.**

These are two separate *hishtalshelus*'s at the same time. The *igulim*, a circle inside a circle, go down to the *sof maaseh*. Alongside, starting after them, come the *sefiros* of *yosher*, like a person in three lines, where the top one is *metzamtzem* and *mislabesh* in the lower one, and the higher keep going into the lower ones as it goes down.

blocks.title: A swimming pool
blocks.text: In *yosher*, first you figure out what you want, like *Atzilus*. Then what that means: if you like to swim, a swimming pool. Then exactly what form, how big and built of what, like *Yetzira*. Then how to build it, like *Asiya*. In *igulim* you also want all that, but the lower you go, the less you care, because it is not your main *ratzon*. That is why people like to daydream: the circles keep getting smaller and farther from the real thing.

In *igulim* it is all a daydream. Imagining yourself digging out the swimming pool is the most fake, farthest from actually doing it; the most real thing is that you want it. But when you finish imagining and say, "Okay, I want to actually do it," you start actually wanting it, and first you figure out what you want.

blocks.title: A swimming pool
blocks.text: "Oh, I'd like to be able to swim" becomes *mislabesh* in the *ratzon* for a swimming pool, and that's it: now you want a swimming pool, not to swim. Swimming you could get at a lake or the beach, but you decided to live in the city and have a pool. Once you decide, the other *ratzonos* are covered over. All you see is the pool, and hidden inside it is the kernel of truth, that you just want to swim. That kernel is the *igul* of *ratzon*, now *metzamtzem* into the *sechel*.

blocks.title: A swimming pool
blocks.text: Then you look through catalogs and see one pool good for your price range, your house, your size. Now those *middos* (*middos* also means dimensions: how big, what it is made of, the price, the specifications) become the main thing, and the general picture of wanting a pool becomes *metzamtzem* and *mislabesh* in them: you want that one. "Yeah, that's what catalogs do. They get you to go from wanting a pool to wanting this pool."

"I see this happen all the time with people." A second ago they were hungry, "I'm in the mood for anything." Then their heart is set on one thing, they get all excited and forget why they wanted it. If it turns out to be a real pain to get, they cannot just get something more practical: "No, I wanted it. Oh, what can I do? Is there some way I can get it?" It becomes a big crisis that they cannot get it the exact way they envisioned. "It's like a little bit of an *akshanus*," a little stubborn.

Then wanting that specific thing becomes *mislabesh* in a *maaseh*. They decide to work to save money, and can get so caught up in the working that they forget why. There is no real *hishtalshelus* in *ratzon*, especially in the *igulim*: a lower *igul* can blow up and become a bigger one. Once you associate a higher stage with a lower one, the lower takes over and becomes the all-encompassing goal, and everything else hides in the background.

blocks.question: Why does yosher look like a person?
blocks.text: There is a *yosher* that does not yet necessarily look like a person. But this is how a person works: the *ratzon* goes into the *sechel*, the *sechel* into the *middos*, the *middos* into the *maaseh*, and it comes out. Since the *ratzon* goes through those human steps, it takes the shape of a person. The *igulim* are like the soul before it comes into the body; *yosher* is the soul in the body, which has to work through the way people work.

In the *igulim* you go through all the steps too, but the *ratzon* stays on top and never becomes *batel* to the *sechel*; the *sechel* is *batel* to it. The *ratzon* bribes the *sechel* to find a reasoning that fits, "you're biased"; the *sechel* bribes the *middos*, and the *middos* bribe the *maaseh*, so you tell yourself you will do "these crazy things" to get the *middos* you want.

*Yosher* is the opposite. The *igulim* are passion-oriented; in *yosher* the orientation is practical, and the top thing becomes the best way to do it. The *maaseh* is the context that defines everything: if it is more practical a certain way, you change the *middos*, the exact form of what you wanted, and that changes the *sechel* and the *ratzon*. Because your main goal is actually to do it, everything has to fit what is practical to do. "That's what it means to be practical."

This is *teshuva* and *maasim tovim* (good deeds): *teshuva* is *igulim*, and *maasim tovim* is *yosher*. These are the two steps, *ratzo* and *shov* (running and returning), *MaH* and *BaN*, which include really everything: the *igulim* are *MaH*, and the *yosher* is *BaN*.

phrases.en: the final thing, the *maaseh b'poel mamash*
inside of the *poel mamash* was *machshava*
and inside that is the *middos*

phrases.he: ובמדות מלובש החכמה ובינה ובחכמה מלובש הרצון והתענוג
ונמצא פנימי מכולם הוא הרצון והתענוג,
phrases.en: the most inner, hidden thing is the *taanug* and the *ratzon*

phrases.he: וחיצון שבכולם הוא המעשה גרוע כו'
phrases.en: and the most external thing, the lowest thing, is the *maaseh*
this is *yosher*

phrases.he: כשבא בבחינת התלבשות העליון בתחתון כו'
phrases.en: when the upper one goes into the lower one

blocks.text: **The final thing, the maaseh b'poel mamash**, includes everything: **inside of the poel mamash was machshava, and inside that is the middos**, in the *middos* *chachma* and *bina*, and in the *chachma* the *ratzon* and *taanug*. So **the most inner, hidden thing is the taanug and the ratzon, and the most external thing, the lowest thing, is the maaseh.** The *maaseh* is now on top, the most outside, what you see. In *igulim* what you see is the *ratzon* and *taanug*, and the *maaseh* is just a representation of it.

"The thought that counts" is the motto of *igulim*: you had good intentions. In *yosher* they say, "Yeah, well, the path to hell is paved with good intentions, my friend. Show me the bottom line." *Maaseh hu ha'ikar* (the deed is the main thing): "I don't care about all your good intentions. Show me the buckaroos." The Frierdiker Rebbe says you need cold, hard cash: *kove'a itim l'Torah* (set times for Torah), actually doing things.

In *yosher* the main thing is the whole point of this week's *parsha*: G-d wants you to do *yosher*. Do not worry about the *igulim*. *Hanistaros la'Hashem Elokeinu v'haniglos lanu ul'vaneinu*: the hidden things are the *igulim*, G-d's business, why He wants it and what He gets out of it. Your business is what He told you: do this, and this will happen. So *ki karov eilecha hadavar me'od, b'ficha uvilvavcha la'asoso*: He told you black on white in the Torah, and the main thing is that you actually do the *mitzvos*, not the spiritual levels. And it is very easy to know whether you did it.

The Torah itself only tells you the bottom line, what it wants. The Oral Torah and the Rabbis tell you what you need to do to get yourself there. The Torah says not to have all these bad relations, so the Rabbis say dress and act with *tznius* (modesty); the Torah does not give those details, because they are not the main *ratzon*, just how to get yourself to do it. "I'm paying you to finish the job. You're the expert, you figure out how to do the job, but I want it to look like this." The behind-the-scenes stuff is theirs; the bottom line is whether you do it.

So it says *Elokim asa es ha'adam yashar*, G-d made man straight, *v'heima bikshu tachbulos*, and they made schemes in *igulim*: "It's true that G-d told us to do this, but I look into the *igulim* and see what He really wants, so maybe I'll do it this way, and He'll like it even better." They try to do better than what He told them.

Which in a way we are going to do, by the way: that is the *inyan* of *teshuva*, doing something better that G-d did not even ask for. But that is also a source of sin, because we are not listening to Him.

**This is yosher, when the upper one goes into the lower one.**

sections.title: The ratzon kadum goes by circles, and comes from the reshimu through a short line
sections.summary: Because the *ratzon kadum* is still for oneself, it goes by way of circles, its first circle the general *makif* of all the worlds. Before it, the beginning of the *Kav* is a short line, one little point that carries the essence and stands for all of it, as a hair comes from the brain; so from the *reshimu*, still infinite though limited, the *Kav* measures out one little *ratzon kadum*.

phrases.en: but in the *ratzon kadum*
it's still within yourself
therefore it goes by way of circles

phrases.en: that top thing, that encompasses everything and defines everything, is this hidden *ratzon*, this all-encompassing desire

which is inside of it

blocks.text: **But in the ratzon kadum, it's still within yourself; therefore it goes by way of circles**: **that top thing, that encompasses everything and defines everything, is this hidden ratzon, this all-encompassing desire**, for yourself. **And the first circle of it is the general ratzon and taanug for the whole hishtalshelus, which is inside of it. And this first igul is the general makif for the entire ABYA.**

phrases.en: and the *reshis hakav*, before this first circle, that little line thing
is a *hiyuli hamshacha*

phrases.he: כמו קו קצר המתצמצם מעילה לעלול,
phrases.en: which is similar to the little line that connects the *ila* to the *alul*
like from *ratzon* to *chachma*; that's just like a little line

blocks.text: **And the reshis hakav**, the little line before this first circle, **is a hiyuli hamshacha** (a raw, general drawing forth), **similar to the little line that connects the ila to the alul**, the cause to the effect.

blocks.title: A hair from the brain
blocks.text: The lower circle does not really reach the upper one; it only represents it. That is the idea of a *kav*, a line, or a hair, wherever it speaks of the *tzimtzum* of hairs and lines: in one small point the *etzem* is carried over, totally *metzumtzam* (contracted), just a representation. The hair comes from the actual stuff of your brain, but it is detached, and you do not see the connection, though there is one. Or a *dugma* (an example): you take one thing to represent the whole thing.

That is a line: you pick one little point of the essence and use it as if it were everything. Your *ratzon* could come out in any way; you pick one *chachma*, one picture out of infinite pictures, and the connection is a little line. So the whole *ratzon kadum*, the desire for a *dira b'tachtonim*, is a little line from the *Atzmus Ein Sof*: one little example of how the *ratzon hamuchlat* could come out.

In the *ratzon hamuchlat* there is no up and down; it is just the taste. That it was set up with ten *sefiros*, with this as the main priority, could have come out in infinite ways, so that too is a little line. The *Kav* is that kind of little line, bringing out a little thing, **like from ratzon to chachma.**

phrases.he: כך מבחינת הרשימו הנזכר לעיל נמשך קו בצמצום גדול מאד
phrases.en: so too from the *reshimu*, which has hidden in it all of G-d's taste of how He would want anything He would ever want and how He would do anything (the whole *Atzmus Ein Sof* is hidden there), comes out one little *ratzon kadum*

phrases.he: דהגם שהרשימו הוא בא בהגבלה כנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: even though we said that the *reshimu* was very limited, it's already like a *metzumtzam* thing

phrases.he: אבל הוא מבחינת עולם האין סוף על כל פנים,
phrases.en: it's still the world of the *Ein Sof*

phrases.he: רק שהוא בחינת האחרונה שנעשה בקיצור כו'
phrases.en: It's just like the end of the *Ein Sof*, which is made like in a short way

blocks.text: **So too from the reshimu**, which hides all of G-d's taste, how He would want anything and do anything, the whole *Atzmus Ein Sof*, now comes out **one little ratzon kadum**, a *kav* in a very great contraction.

**Even though we said that the reshimu was very limited**, **it's still the world of the Ein Sof.** "So a zero in the world of the *Ein Sof* is more infinite than an infinity in the world of an *igul*." The *Atzmus Ein Sof* is like a guy with a *ratzon hamuchlat*, a taste, already the last level, *Kadmon*: He chose to reveal Himself in a certain way.

But even that particular way, *Kadmon*, is still a taste, totally infinite compared to coming out into the world. In *Kadmon* He picks a taste because He feels Himself in that style. When He is *metzamtzem* it into a *reshimu*, He hides Himself: all that is left are the choices of His style and taste, without seeing Him in them. That is the *reshimu*.

Yet all that is still far more infinite than any particular *hishtalshelus*, like making a house, because there is no up and down yet: you could want the whole house for the bathroom drapes. In the *reshimu* he already knows; ask him, "How would you want your house?" and he can tell you. But to actually want a house you need the *tzimtzum* of the *Kav*, which pulls out and measures which thing comes out and in what order.

The *Kav* measured out that he will want a house, as the main thing, with the details and what it takes to get it secondary: "Okay, so I want a home. That's my goal." That automatically includes wanting whatever he will need to get it. Then it goes to *yosher*: when he actually decides, he gets a job and works, whatever it takes to get a home.

The *Kav* is *chozer u'meir*: it reveals the light again a little. The *Kav* always means your choice, so it reveals you: you are choosing which way to bring it out, measuring it, and you see that you are measuring.

blocks.title: The teacher
blocks.text: In the *mashal* of the teacher, the *reshimu* is all the knowledge in his memory, facts in a way separate from him: there is him, and there are the things he knows. When he is not thinking about them, they are there in a hidden way, and you do not see his mind in them. The *Kav* is that he measures out which students and subjects he teaches and which explanations to bring out. Those explanations were measured by him, so you see a kind of *gilui ohr* (revealed light), revealed in his mind.

blocks.title: The teacher
blocks.text: A person thinking about deep things, all his understanding in play, makes a *tzimtzum*: he clears his mind and gives his full attention to the students. Then he takes out his *kav*, measures the students, and chooses what to bring out and in what order, an idea they will understand. He picks the *meshalim*: tennis for the guy who likes tennis, hunting for the hunter, cars for the car guy. He picks the idea for the student's level, the *kelim* (vessels) of explanation and the *meshalim*, and puts it all together.

blocks.text: The *Atzmus* is not a desire to do something; it is just to be yourself. Deciding you want to be someone who does something is the *sof maaseh* of the *machshava* of the *Ein Sof*, the end of *Kadmon*: you associate yourself with doing things a certain way, to express yourself. You want to leave an impression of yourself in the world, a *reshimu*. You make the *tzimtzum* to make a *gilui* that is separate from you and yet reflects on you: that you chose this idea to come out this way reveals you.

blocks.title: A painter's signature
blocks.text: That is your choice: you pick a style or a taste, and anything done that way is like a signature. Each painter has his character; you take one look and say, "Oh, I know who did that." That is a *reshimu*, an imprint left from the person.

blocks.title: The teacher
blocks.text: In a teacher, the desire to teach is the desire for a *reshimu*: to leave an impression of your intellect in somebody else's mind. So you hide your intellect and reveal the *koach hagvul* (the power of limitation), making it into ideas as if separate from you. Really it is you; you cannot separate the ideas from the person who thought them up. But you make it as if separate, and then you can give it over to somebody else.

blocks.text: Even though the *reshimu* comes in a limited way, it is still of the *Atzmus Ein Sof*. It is the *koach hagvul* of the *Ein Sof*, and still infinite: every possible limited thing G-d could make that could seem separate, not one particular *gvul* (limit) but every possible *gvul*. **It's just like the end of the Ein Sof, which is made like in a short way.** But it is still infinite.

blocks.text: **But to have the ratzon kadum, which is already outside of the world of the Ein Sof**: you already chose one particular *ratzon* for this *hishtalshelus*. **Even though the ratzon kadum is a hiyuli that includes everything** in our world, it is already a *prat* outside the *Atzmus*.

**Therefore, it has to come through a short Kav.** To jump from the *reshimu* of the *koach*, at the end of the *Ein Sof*, to the beginning of the *hishtalshelus*, it has to come as a little *kav*, finite: one little thing picked out to represent the whole *etzem*.

blocks.question: Is the kav katzar itself the ratzon kadum?
blocks.text: No. The *kav katzar* (the short line) is from chapters 14 and 15; the first *igul* the *Kav* makes is the *ratzon kadum*. For it to come out of the *ratzon hamuchlat* you need the *tzimtzum*, which leaves the *reshimu*, and then the *Kav*. The first *igul* has many names: the great *igul*, the *ratzon kadum*, the general *makif* of *Beriya*, sometimes the *machshava kduma* of *Adam Kadmon*.

sections.title: Up and down begin with the Kav; of the Essence above it nothing can be said
sections.summary: The *Kav* only makes an up and a down, taking one little detail of the will and connecting it to *chachma*. In the world of the *Ein Sof* there is no up and down, only simple unity, the way a person's taste is the person; so it cannot be spoken of, and only the *Kav* and *Adam Kadmon*, the cause of all causes, can be grasped. The *tzimtzum* is a jump, not a line, which is why the Essence is called holy, and why *Adam Kadmon* is a man while of the Essence it says, "He is not a man."

It does this by taking one little *prat* of the *ratzon* and connecting it to the *chachma*, so the *chachma* represents just this one little *prat* of the *Keser*.

blocks.text: **But in the world of the Ein Sof**, with none of that *Kav* business, **there's not even an up and down.** Even with all the *tzimtzumim* it stays all on one level, totally infinite, the *Atzmus* of the *Ein Sof*.

**It's just completely an achdus pshuta** (simple unity), **one simple thing**: the *gilui* of G-d exactly as He is. In you, it is just you: your taste is you. Books about style in writing will all tell you that the style is the person; it is not a separate thing.

**Even though He estimated what's going to be**, like a taste, **it's all within yourself.** You were not thinking of the particular things to come; you chose a taste for yourself, which is really you, deciding what kind of person you will be. That **is still completely infinite.**

blocks.text: **Therefore it says in Etz Chaim: even Malchus of Ein Sof you can't really speak about.** There is no way to describe it, because you would need physical terms, and it is totally infinite; you cannot limit it to any kind of thing.

blocks.title: Trying to explain style
blocks.text: That is why they have so much trouble explaining style. All they can tell you is: if you want to get it out, do not think about it. Think about the *sof maaseh*, and it will come out *mimeila* (by itself), because it is you. If you try to bring it out, you cover it up and make a *kelipa* (a husk) over it.

blocks.text: **But Atzmus Ein Sof, no thought can grasp it**, even the *machshava kduma*: the first thought of the *ratzon kadum* does not capture the *Atzmus* at all. **The Ein Sof is totally separate. It's called completely kadosh** (holy). Why *kadosh*? **Because of the tzimtzum.**

So there is no *kav* connecting them: from before the *tzimtzum* to after it is a jump, not a line. Everywhere else He picks one little part of what He wants to reveal and makes that like everything: one swimming pool, one shape, one material, a little thing of the *etzem*. In the first *tzimtzum* you hid everything: "You went from being you to being something outside of you, and that's it." You hid yourself; you did not pick a little thing of yourself.

blocks.text: But **the ratzon kadum is called His great name**: *shmo* (His name) has the *gematria* (numerical value) of *ratzon*; **in other words, it's His big desire.** And this is the meaning of *Yehei shmei rabba mevarach*.

If you have the *kavana* you are supposed to have in *Yehei shmei rabba mevarach*, it tears up decrees of seventy years. The *kavana* is that G-d's great name be drawn down into the world. His great name is the *ratzon* for the *dira b'tachtonim*, for *Moshiach*. So connecting to that *ratzon*, the spreading of the wellsprings, tears up all decrees, because that is the main goal.

blocks.text: As is known, **Adam Kadmon is called Adam d'Beriya**, as will be explained. **But about Atzmus Ein Sof it says ki lo adam hu: it's not a person.** As is known from the *kavanos* of *Nishmas Kol Chai*, **Adam Kadmon is already like a thing of a person, and it's like the soul of creation**; higher than that you cannot call it a person at all, because that was a total jump.

reviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between *igulim* and *yosher*, and how does drawing the circles without lifting the pen show what the beginning of the *Kav* does?
In what sense is the *ratzon kadum* already revealed, and in what sense is it still hidden? What do the teenager whose parents cramp his style and the song in your head show?
Why does every last detail, the bathroom drapes or a blade of grass, matter to the first will, and in what way is the last deed first in thought?
Why can the reasons never reach the will? Explain with the kid who wants a bike and with the bribe.
What changes when the will for oneself comes to be done in actual fact, and why does the *sof maaseh* go from the flimsiest circle to the top?
Why can even *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* not be spoken of, and why is the *tzimtzum* called a jump and not a line?
